verdict.rationale: DBOS docs explicitly describe workflows waiting hours-to-days for human input via DBOS.recv(timeout_seconds=...) surviving process restarts and server upgrades, backed by Postgres checkpointing rather than any held server/connection (dbos-docs-12, dbos-docs-28, dbos-docs-39, dbos-docs-2, dbos-docs-4). The architecture is confirmed as a library with no dedicated orchestration server, only Postgres, so a sleeping workflow consumes no compute (dbos-docs-2, dbos-docs-20, dbos-docs-35). missing for 10: explicit mention of multi-month sleep durations (only 'hours or days' is documented), and independent/third-party confirmation of zero billable compute during long sleeps.
